correctness.rationale: For any distinct a,b in a connected set K, point separation gives a continuous real-linear scalar functional f with f(a) != f(b). Continuity yields |f(x)-f(y)| <= C||x-y|| = C d_p(x,y)^(1/p), so f|K is 1/p-Hölder. The connected nonconstant image f(K) contains a nondegenerate interval and therefore has Hausdorff dimension at least one; the standard Hölder covering inequality gives dim_H f(K) <= p dim_H K, hence dim_H K >= 1/p. Every nontrivial affine segment has metric equal, up to scale, to |s-t|^p and therefore has dimension exactly 1/p. In L_p[0,1], t -> 1_[0,t] has d_p-distance exactly |s-t|, so it realizes dimension one, while every nondegenerate connected metric space has Hausdorff dimension at least one. The complete relevant metric-rigidity section of the primary p-Banach source was independently read and confirms the point-separating snowflake setting and the contrasting L_p indicator path.
